title: Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: All directors, executives, officers, employees, contractors and consultants of the Company. Subject to the inside-information ban, the Front Page Test, the short-term/speculative dealing ban and the Hedging rules; not subject to blackout periods or pre-clearance unless also a Restricted Person.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Directors, Senior Executives and Nominated Employees. Subject to additional restrictions: no dealing in blackout periods, prior approval required for dealing outside blackout periods, margin lending approval, trade confirmation, and a duty to police dealings by their Connected Persons.

tiers.name: Senior Executives
tiers.description: Direct reports to the CEO and key management personnel who have been advised by the Chief Legal Officer & Secretary that they are subject to special restrictions; a category of Restricted Person distinguished for clearance approver (CEO).

tiers.name: Nominated Employees
tiers.description: Employees who regularly possess inside information and have been advised by the Chief Legal Officer & Secretary that they are subject to special restrictions; a category of Restricted Person distinguished for clearance approver (CEO).

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Company; a category of Restricted Person distinguished for clearance approver (Chair of the Board) and for same-day trade confirmation to assist disclosure compliance.

tiers.name: CEO
tiers.description: The Chief Executive Officer; distinguished for clearance approver (Chair of the Board) and as a Reporting Person under Section 16(b) of the US Exchange Act.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: The Chair of the Board; distinguished for clearance approver (Chair of the Audit, Governance and Risk Committee).

tiers.name: Reporting Persons
tiers.description: The CEO and his/her direct reports, Directors, and any holder of 10% or more of the Company's issued and outstanding securities; subject to the US Exchange Act Section 16(b) short-swing profit prohibition in addition to the general short-term dealing ban.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: A family member who may be expected to influence, or be influenced by, the Restricted Person (spouse, partner, children, partner's children, dependents), and any company or other entity the Restricted Person can control; excludes EMG and the Seller Group Entities.

definitions.hedging_definition: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities.

windows.start_anchor: 15th day of the third month of each calendar quarter
windows.end_anchor: completion of the two trading days following the public release by the Company of quarterly or annual earnings

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board or the Chief Legal Officer & Secretary may specify any other period as a blackout period from time to time. A refused or revoked individual clearance request must be kept confidential; the imposition of an ad hoc blackout period itself is not stated to be confidential.

rules.detail: 'Securities' includes any other financial product of the Company quoted on the ASX or another exchange, so an exchange-quoted, Company-issued derivative is a security; dealing in it follows the ordinary framework (blackout periods and prior approval for Restricted Persons, inside-information ban for all).
rules.evidence: a reference to "securities" means securities in the Company and any other financial products of the Company quoted on the ASX or any other exchange or marketplace.

rules.detail: A third-party OTC derivative (e.g. a bank-written put or call) is not 'of the Company' and is not quoted, so it falls outside the 'securities' definition and the ordinary dealing framework; it is caught only if it operates to limit the economic risk of holding Company securities, in which case the Hedging rules apply instead.
Absolute ban, applying to all Employees (not only Restricted Persons), on hedging Company securities acquired under an equity plan before they vest.
rules.evidence: Company securities acquired under an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company must never be hedged prior to vesting.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging Company securities while subject to a holding lock or dealing restriction under an equity plan, even once vested.
rules.evidence: Company securities must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company.

rules.detail: Once vested and free of any holding lock, hedging is not banned but is caught by the Hedging definition ('arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities'); as a Restricted Person the individual must obtain prior approval to deal outside a blackout period and cannot deal inside one absent an exceptional-circumstances approval. It is not explicit whether an OTC hedge (not itself a 'security' under section 1) technically requires 4.3 approval, or is regulated only by the freestanding 3.4 ban/permission.
rules.evidence: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities.

rules.detail: For Employees who are not Restricted Persons, hedging of vested, unrestricted Company securities is not banned and no blackout or pre-clearance regime applies under this Policy, though the inside-information ban, Front Page Test and speculative/short-term dealing ban continue to apply.
rules.evidence: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A structure that limits the economic risk of holding Company securities (e.g. a prepaid forward) falls within the Hedging definition and follows the ordinary approval/blackout framework; a structure that is instead an outright agreement to sell the underlying shares is an ordinary Dealing.
rules.evidence: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named, but as an inherently speculative strategy it falls within the ban on speculative or short-term dealing.
rules.evidence: Employees must not deal in the Company's securities on a speculative or short-term trading basis.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.

CFDs are not named. As an instrument for speculative trading in the Company's securities they fall within the ban on speculative or short-term dealing; if instead used to limit the economic risk of an existing holding, they would fall within the Hedging rules.
rules.evidence: Employees must not deal in the Company's securities on a speculative or short-term trading basis.

rules.detail: A Restricted Person must obtain approval under the 4.4 process before entering into a margin lending arrangement over Company securities or transferring Company securities into an existing margin loan account.
rules.evidence: Approval must be obtained by any Restricted Person in accordance with the procedure set out in section 4.4 for any: (1) entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities; and (2) transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account.

rules.detail: The margin lending approval requirement applies only to Restricted Persons; for other Employees, entering a margin loan or transferring Company securities into one is not restricted by this Policy.
rules.evidence: Approval must be obtained by any Restricted Person in accordance with the procedure set out in section 4.4 for any: (1) entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities

rules.detail: Granting security over Company securities is not separately named; it is closely analogous to, and likely swept in by, the express margin lending approval requirement, though a charge given otherwise than in connection with a margin loan is not explicitly addressed.
rules.evidence: Approval must be obtained by any Restricted Person in accordance with the procedure set out in section 4.4 for any: (1) entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities; and (2) transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account.

rules.detail: Only 'margin lending arrangements' are named. A bank loan secured on the collared shares that is not documented as a conventional margin loan is not explicitly covered, but given its identical economic effect it should be treated as requiring the same 4.4 clearance out of caution.
rules.evidence: Approval must be obtained by any Restricted Person in accordance with the procedure set out in section 4.4 for any: (1) entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities; and (2) transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account.

rules.detail: Ban on speculative or short-term dealing, defined as buying and selling securities on market within a 6 month period, and entering into other short-term dealings such as forward contracts; sale of shares converted after exercising options or rights may not be regarded as short-term trading.
rules.evidence: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 6 month period and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

rules.detail: US Exchange Act Section 16(b) short-swing profit rule applies specifically to the CEO and his/her direct reports, directors and any holder of 10% or more of the Company's securities, prohibiting matching purchases and sales within 6 months regardless of intent.
rules.evidence: Specifically prohibited are purchases and sales of Company securities that are subject to Section 16(b) of the Exchange Act by the CEO and his/her direct reports, directors and any holder of 10% or more of the Company's issued and outstanding securities (collectively a "Reporting Person").

exceptions.evidence: participation in an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company. However, where securities in the Company granted under an employee, executive or director equity plan cease to be held under the terms of that plan, any dealings in those securities must only occur in accordance with this Policy;

dealings that result in no effective change to the beneficial interest in the securities (for example, transfers of Company securities already held into a superannuation fund or trust of which the Employee is a beneficiary);

trading under a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan, where the Employee did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a blackout period, the plan does not permit the Employee to exercise any influence or discretion in relation to trading under the plan and the plan cannot be cancelled during a blackout period, other than in exceptional circumstances.

exceptions.approver: routed under section 4.4 (CEO / Chair of the Board / Chair of the Audit, Governance and Risk Committee)
exceptions.evidence: If a director or salaried employee needs to deal in securities during a blackout period due to exceptional circumstances and is not in possession of any Inside Information, then, they may apply for approval to deal in accordance with section 4.4. Exceptional circumstances are likely to include severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order.

exceptions.approver: routed under section 4.4 (CEO / Chair of the Board / Chair of the Audit, Governance and Risk Committee)
exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances are likely to include severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order.

financing_disclosure: Restricted Persons: at inception, before entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of Company securities or transferring Company securities into an existing margin loan account, to the routed approver under section 4.4 (CEO, Chair of the Board, or Chair of the Audit, Governance and Risk Committee); approval required before proceeding.

exemption_authority: A Restricted Person needing to deal during a blackout period due to severe financial hardship, compulsion by court order, or other exceptional circumstances (and who is not in possession of Inside Information) may apply for approval via the section 4.4 process to the same routed approver (CEO, Chair of the Board, or Chair of the Audit, Governance and Risk Committee). Approval is entirely discretionary, need not be accompanied by reasons, may be made subject to conditions, and may be revoked at any time; a refusal or revocation must be kept confidential.
jurisdiction_overlays: US Securities Exchange Act of 1934, including the Section 16(b) short-swing profit rule applicable to the CEO, direct reports, Directors and 10%+ holders

bespoke_clauses.clause: a reference to "securities" means securities in the Company and any other financial products of the Company quoted on the ASX or any other exchange or marketplace.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank-written OTC put and call referencing Coronado shares is not 'of the Company' and not quoted, so it falls outside the Policy's own 'securities'/'dealing' definitions; it is caught only via the separate, broader Hedging definition, leaving genuine doubt whether the blackout and 4.3 pre-clearance regime technically extends to it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Approval must be obtained by any Restricted Person in accordance with the procedure set out in section 4.4 for any: entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities; and transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar should be treated as requiring the same 4.4 approval as a conventional margin lending arrangement, even though a bespoke bank loan not documented via a margin account is not literally within the clause's wording.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Specifically prohibited are purchases and sales of Company securities that are subject to Section 16(b) of the Exchange Act by the CEO and his/her direct reports, directors and any holder of 10% or more of the Company's issued and outstanding securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For US-reporting insiders, any matching purchase and sale (or sale and purchase) within 6 months - potentially including collar unwind and rebuild - risks disgorgement of profit under Section 16(b), independently of this Policy's clearance process.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Following receipt of approval to deal, the approved dealing must occur within 5 business days following approval (or such other time specified in the approval), otherwise the approval is no longer effective, and a new approval must be sought. ... [The approver] may revoke their approval at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar must be executed within 5 business days of approval and remains subject to unilateral revocation by the approver at any time before execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In the case of Directors, written confirmation should ideally be provided by close of business on the day the trade is entered into to assist the Company to comply with its disclosure obligations under the Exchange Act and ASX Listing Rules.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A Director's collar trade needs same-day reporting to the Chief Legal Officer & Secretary to meet dual US/ASX disclosure timelines.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees and directors must take appropriate steps to ensure that their "Connected Persons" only deal in securities in circumstances where the Restricted Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to deal under this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, partner or a controlled entity does not avoid the blackout, clearance, hedging or margin lending restrictions.

summary: A funded collar sits in a genuine grey zone here: the Policy's own 'securities' definition is limited to Company-issued products quoted on an exchange, so a bilateral OTC put and call written by a bank is arguably not 'dealing in the Company's securities' triggering the ordinary blackout/pre-clearance regime, but it squarely falls within the separate Hedging definition ('arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities'), which absolutely bans hedging of unvested or holding-locked plan securities and, once vested and unrestricted, should be treated as requiring the same prior approval Restricted Persons need for any dealing (from the CEO, Chair of the Board, or Chair of the Audit, Governance and Risk Committee depending on seniority) outside a blackout period. The loan leg is expressly regulated only as a 'margin lending arrangement', which needs prior approval from the same approver before the Restricted Person enters into it or transfers Company shares into an existing margin account; a bespoke bank loan not styled as a margin loan is not explicitly covered but should be cleared out of caution given its identical economic effect. Approval, once given, lapses if the trade is not executed within 5 business days, may be conditioned or revoked at any time, and a refusal must be kept confidential; the Restricted Person must promptly (same-day for Directors) confirm the completed trade to the Chief Legal Officer & Secretary. For US-reporting insiders (the CEO and direct reports, Directors, and 10%+ holders), Section 16(b) additionally exposes any matching purchase and sale within 6 months to disgorgement, which is relevant to collar unwind and rebuild. Overall: proceed only with prior written approval for both the derivative and financing legs, executed and documented outside any blackout period.
